package_info.why_malicious: The report discusses ransomware as a threat vector, including the use of malicious open source packages to deliver ransomware payloads. However, it does not provide details about any specific malicious package, its name, version, or code. The macro-level reasoning is that attackers may use compromised or intentionally malicious open source packages to deliver ransomware, exploiting software vulnerabilities as an entry point.

behavioral_signatures: Open source package performing unexpected encryption of user files
Package initiating network connections to command-and-control servers
Package attempting to exfiltrate sensitive data or credentials
Package executing system-level commands to disable backups or security tools
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious binaries/scripts in node_modules or site-packages
Unexpected modifications to user files or system configuration files
Creation of ransom note files (e.g., README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt, HOW_TO_DECRYPT.html)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ransomware C2 domains or IPs
Unusual traffic to cryptocurrency payment addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for open source packages that perform file encryption, spawn suspicious child processes, or initiate outbound network connections to untrusted domains. Flag packages that access or modify large numbers of files, especially outside their expected scope. Look for the creation of ransom note files or attempts to disable security tools. Use threat intelligence to correlate network activity with known ransomware infrastructure.
